newsitem.title: JAPAN: Three Japan oil firms to jointly procure goods.
newsitem.headline: Three Japan oil firms to jointly procure goods.

text.p: Three Japanese oil firms, all affiliated to major U.S. oil firm Exxon Corp, said on Wednesday they would jointly purchase refinery facility parts and product materials in a bid to slash costs.
Esso Sekiyu K.K., Tonen Corp and General Sekiyu KK said they would start cooperation on October 1, aiming to cut costs spent on purchasing various goods by 10 percent by 2000.
"In the initial year of cooperation, each firm is expected to cut about 200 million to 500 million yen in costs," a spokesman for Tonen Corp said.
Japanese oil firms have been striving to cut costs, as revenue from gasoline sales, previously a main source of their income, has tumbled together with retail prices.
Exxon Corp fully owns Esso Sekiyu and has a 25 percent stake in Tonen Corp and a 47.47 percent stake in General Sekiyu.
